summary:
The agreement sets AtliQ to design, build, deploy and support a revenue‑management platform for nine Saudi hotels, includes on‑site project‑manager duties, training for up to 40 staff, and defines handling of guest personal data. Risks include potentially uncapped support obligations, on‑site staffing costs, extensive training scope, and the need to confirm data‑privacy compliance.

Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts · MSA · AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd as supplier. 12 finding(s): 1 critical, 3 high, 7 medium, 1 low; 2 potential conflict(s) with past commitments; 1 check(s) could not be verified.

findings.title: Potential conflict with Al Noor Hospitality Group non-compete (§12.1)
findings.explanation: Potential conflict — not a breach determination. Al Noor Hospitality Group §12.1: No data analytics, AI or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business (hotel owners/operators, or distribution / revenue-management / guest-analytics providers to hotels) headquartered in, or for properties in, the GCC (UAE, KSA, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman). Status: active, until 14 Sep 2029 (Term ends 14 Mar 2028 (§6.1) + 18-month Restricted Period ≈ 14 Sep 2029.). The restriction binds AtliQ's Affiliates too, so signing through the other AtliQ entity does not avoid it. This contract matches every element — hospitality sector: hotels, resorts, hotel, resort · GCC geography: Saudi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Al Khobar, Madinah · analytics / AI / revenue-management services: analytics, artificial intelligence, revenue management, models, forecasting. Related: waiver (spent) — One-off consent under §12.4 for the Seaside Hotels (Muscat) demand-forecasting SOW only. Excludes extensions, any other Hospitality Business and all AtliQ Affiliates.
findings.contract_quote: The Service Provider shall design, develop, test, deploy and support a revenue management and guest analytics platform for the Company's nine (9) Properties located in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as listed in Schedule 2.

evidence.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
evidence.label: Signed: al noor hospitality msa §12.1 (Active until 14 Sep 2029)

evidence.quote: "Hospitality Business" means any person, firm or entity that owns, operates, manages or franchises hotels, resorts or serviced apartments, or that provides distribution, revenue-management or guest-analytics services to any such person, firm or entity.

services are provided "in the GCC" if the Hospitality Business receiving them is headquartered in, or the services relate to properties or operations located in, any state of the GCC, irrespective of where the services are performed.
The Supplier shall procure that each of its Affiliates complies with this Clause 12 as if it were a party to this Agreement, and any breach by an Affiliate shall be deemed a breach by the Supplier.
"Restricted Period" means the Term and the period of eighteen (18) months following the expiry or termination of this Agreement.

This consent is strictly limited to the Seaside SOW. It does not extend to (a) any other services provided to Seaside, including any extension, renewal, change order or follow-on statement of work, unless separately consented to in writing by the Client; (b) any other Hospitality Business, whether in the Sultanate of Oman or elsewhere in the GCC; or (c) any Affiliate of the Supplier.
evidence.label: Signed: al noor waiver letter ¶2–3 (Spent)

findings.title: No cap on direct liability
findings.explanation: Clause 10.1 limits only indirect losses and does not cap AtliQ's direct liability, exposing the company to unlimited damages for breach or negligence.
findings.contract_quote: Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, special or consequential loss, or loss of profits, arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

findings.title: Liquidated damages on the full contract value with no client-delay exclusion
findings.explanation: Delay clause terms: one percent (1%) of Contract Value per week, capped, no exclusion for client-caused delay. AtliQ's precedent is 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone, with no LD for client-caused delay (Acme Mar 2025, Northwind Jun 2025, Trustline Aug 2026). Calculating LD on the whole contract value rather than the delayed milestone multiplies exposure. Nothing stops LD accruing while AtliQ waits on the client's own data or access. The only accepted 10%-of-total cap (Al Noor) was approved as a one-off exception, not a standard.
findings.contract_quote: Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.

findings.title: Saudi Arabia law, Arabic text prevails and local courts
findings.explanation: AtliQ's default is Indian law for Pvt Ltd and US state law for Inc. Saudi Arabia is the counterparty's home law, which AtliQ has accepted before when needed (English law for Northwind, DIFC for Al Noor, Singapore/SIAC for CloudSpan). The Arabic version prevails over the English text AtliQ will review — get the governing-language version checked. Forum: Failing amicable resolution, the dispute shall be referred to the competent courts in the City of Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, which shall have exclusive ju (§14.3). Disputes would be run under unfamiliar law, typically needing local counsel.
findings.contract_quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

evidence.quote: In the event of any inconsistency, the Arabic text shall prevail.
